2. The Manager owns the operating framework for storage and distribution of packed consumer goods for about twenty regular clients. This includes the fixed six-zone layout A to F, the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15, staffing of around 38–40 people across two shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, and the standards that system stock is rack stock. No change to zones, procedures or operating hours is valid without the Manager's authorisation.

3. The Manager leads the management team of 2 shift supervisors and 2 dispatchers and, through them, the floor roles: 8 forklift operators, 6 inbound operators, 10 pickers, 2 stock controllers, 4 returns and packing staff, 1 maintenance technician and 2 floaters. The Manager sets rosters, task boundaries and escalation lines, and ensures every person works only within role, training and authorisation.

4. The Manager holds all final sign-offs for inventory. The Manager plans and orders the annual wall-to-wall stocktake covering all locations in Zones B, C, D, E and F, freezes movements and dock bookings for the count window, and personally signs off the stocktake results by name and date after review of first and second counts, quarantine moves and adjustment proposals.

5. The Manager holds the senior financial control for damaged goods. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the Warehouse Manager, after quarantine in Zone F, inspection, second count and documentation under PR-09. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor, and no damaged goods leave quarantine without the required recorded approval.

6. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime. This includes exceptional Saturday morning overtime in peak season and any extension beyond the rostered 06:00–14:00 and 14:00–22:00 shifts. No supervisor, dispatcher or operator authorises additional hours, and unapproved hours are not worked or paid as overtime.

7. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators under the rule of no licence, no truck. Authorisation covers the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays, and electric pallet jacks, is type-specific and recorded by name, date, truck types and licence evidence. No other person grants, extends or renews driving permission.

8. The Manager is accountable for safety and compliance on site. This includes enforcement of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, pedestrian separation on 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, storage limits of 1,000 kg per pallet, 2,700 kg per rack bay, 3 high and 4.0 m for block stacks, and 4,000 kg for the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, cold-chain discipline at +2 °C to +8 °C, and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence.

9. The Manager supervises through records and review. The Manager reviews shift handover records under PR-15, daily cycle-count accuracy with no adjustment without a second count, monthly racking inspections, temperature and maintenance logs, dock scheduling by the dispatcher, and every escalated incident report. Corrective action to operation, retraining or withdrawal of authorisation is ordered by the Manager.

10. If any instruction in manuals or procedures differs from how the site is actually run, the owner's brief prevails. The Warehouse Manager orders correction of the manual, owns the procedure system PR-01 to PR-15, and is the point of contact for clients, authorities and auditors on operations, safety and inventory assurance.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. The Shift Supervisors are 2 posts covering the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus rostered cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. On every shift there is one named shift supervisor in charge of the floor, identified at shift start and reachable on the floor throughout the shift.

2. The shift supervisor in charge runs the shift. The supervisor allocates tasks at shift start to inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, dispatch support and floaters, sequences put-away from Zone A, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C before picking, transfer to Zone D and loading at doors 1–8, and hands over formally to the next supervisor under PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

3. The supervisor is responsible for order, discipline and safety on the floor and at the dock and yard interface. This includes enforcement of 10 km/h inside the hall, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, use of 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear, seat-belt use, aisle discipline on 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, and correct inbound-outbound use of doors 1–4 and 5–8.

4. The supervisor controls storage and handling discipline during the shift. The supervisor stops put-away to any rack bay above 2,700 kg, any block stack above 3 pallets high or 4.0 m, any pallet above 1,000 kg including load, and any unstable or damaged pallet, orders quarantine in Zone F the same day damage is found, and secures the bay or area until cleared and logged by the maintenance technician.

5. The supervisor ensures shift controls are completed and recorded. This includes replenished pick faces in Zone C before picking starts, daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule with no adjustment without a second count, manual temperature verification in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C each shift, cage quantity against the 4,000 kg limit in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, and documented checks of every truck before its first use each day.

6. The shift supervisor leads incident response on the shift. On injury, near miss, impact, spill, leak, temperature or fire alarm, the supervisor stops work in the affected aisle, bay, zone or dock, secures the area, directs floor staff and drivers in the marked waiting area, ensures Zone E and hazmat-cage attendance is checked, orders evacuation to the assembly point by the north fence with roll call where required, and escalates without delay to the Warehouse Manager.

7. The supervisor exercises defined delegated approvals. The supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR under PR-09, approves the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap on proposal from returns staff under PR-07, orders second counts and quarantine moves, and reviews every incident report before close or escalation.

8. The supervisor does not hold manager-reserved authorities. The supervisor does not approve overtime, does not authorise new forklift operators under the no licence, no truck rule, does not sign off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake, and does not approve write-offs above 500 EUR. Requests for overtime, authorisation or senior write-off are referred to the Warehouse Manager.

9. The line of authority on the shift is fixed. Floor staff report to the shift supervisor in charge, and dispatchers, stock controllers and the maintenance technician work within their roles but remain under the supervisor's floor authority for safety, traffic and sequencing. Escalation runs from supervisor to Warehouse Manager unless immediate escalation is required for injury or evacuation.

10. The handover closes the shift. The outgoing supervisor records by name, date and shift staffing, doors and slots handled, Zone A to F status, WMS tasks open or suspended, counts and recounts outstanding, quarantine and hazmat position, incidents, defects and tagged-out trucks, and confirms receipt by the incoming supervisor. Verbal-only handover is forbidden, and unfinished items are carried by name until closed.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. The Dispatchers are 2 posts working from the office annex and the Zone D interface across the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They own transport booking, dock allocation and outbound load release for the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 fenced yard.

2. The dispatcher books all transport in advance with the carrier. Each booking records carrier name, trailer or van reference, client, expected pallet count and weight, cold-chain or hazmat flag, and assigned door and fixed time slot. No inbound truck arrives at doors 1–4 and no outbound truck arrives at doors 5–8 without a dispatcher booking.

3. The dispatcher assigns every carrier a specific dock door and time slot and owns dock scheduling. Doors 1–4 are inbound only serving Zone A receiving and doors 5–8 are outbound only serving Zone D dispatch, all at 1.2 m dock height with own leveller. No other role changes doors or slots, and the dispatcher sequences arrivals to avoid yard congestion and to keep Zone A clear.

4. The dispatcher instructs drivers on door, slot, site speed limits and waiting rules at booking. In the yard drivers keep to marked lanes at 15 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, report at the assigned door with documents, then wait in the marked waiting area. Drivers never enter the hall, never operate forklifts, jacks, levellers or WMS scanners.

5. The dispatcher flags special goods at booking so the shift team can prepare. Chilled goods for Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C are flagged for priority check in Zone A and direct put-away, and hazardous packed goods for the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage are flagged for segregated check and escorted put-away within its 4,000 kg limit. Documents are checked before anything is unloaded under PR-01.

6. The dispatcher owns load and capacity discipline under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Planning is built on 1,000 kg per pallet including load: contracted curtain-side trailers take 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions, so 24 full-weight pallets by weight, and the delivery van takes 1,200 kg on 6 positions, so one full-weight pallet only. Anything heavier than the van rating goes by trailer.

7. The dispatcher plans outbound throughput to dock capacity. With 4 outbound doors each handling at most 3 trailer loads per shift, the most promised to clients is 288 full-weight pallets per shift. No booking, commitment or release exceeds trailer, van or shift limits, and excess is replanned to the next slot or trailer with the shift supervisor in charge.

8. The dispatcher directs staging and releases outbound loads. Only wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic wrappers, labelled pallets assigned to the load are staged in the 900 m2 Zone D by door and by load on WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners. No truck at doors 5–8 is loaded or sealed until the dispatcher has released the load after weight, count and staging agree.

9. The dispatcher works under the floor authority of the shift supervisor in charge for safety, traffic and sequencing, while retaining scheduling and release authority. The dispatcher coordinates put-away from Zone A, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C and transfer to Zone D with the supervisor, stops early or partial loading before release, and escalates deviations, missed slots, damage or door blocks through the supervisor to the Warehouse Manager.

10. The dispatcher closes and hands over by name under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Bookings made, doors and slots handled, loads released, sealed with seal numbers recorded, incomplete loads and re-bookings, and scanner or leveller faults are recorded by door, load and shift. The dispatcher does not approve overtime, does not authorise forklift operators, and does not approve write-offs, and wears high-visibility vest and class S3 footwear at the dock interface.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. The Inbound Operators are 6 posts working in Zone A receiving of 800 m2 at inbound docks 1-4 across the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They report to the shift supervisor in charge and work to dispatcher bookings and WMS tasks under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

2. The inbound operator unloads only after documents have been checked. On arrival at the assigned door at 1.2 m dock height the operator compares delivery note and transport papers against the dispatcher booking — carrier, client, reference, pallet and carton count, product, batch and expiry, cold-chain or hazmat flag — and starts unloading only when the check is passed and door, leveller and Zone A space are confirmed.

3. If documents are missing, incomplete or do not match the booking, the operator holds the load at the dock. The process is stopped, the shift supervisor and dispatcher are informed at once, and nothing is unloaded and nothing moves past Zone A until the paperwork is resolved and recorded.

4. Unloading is carried out with trained handling discipline in Zone A. Goods are placed staged by delivery clear of levellers, 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area in the yard and never enter the hall or operate equipment, and heavy pallet moves are left to authorised forklift operators on checked electric trucks.

5. Every delivery is counted in Zone A before booking. The operator counts pallets, cartons and units against the checked documents, scans labels on the 20 handheld WMS scanners where required, and records overages, shortages and seal or packaging exceptions on the inbound record. Uncounted goods are never presented for booking.

6. Every delivery is inspected in Zone A before booking. The operator checks outer packaging, pallet condition and stability within the 1,000 kg per pallet limit, labelling and batch marking, visible damage, leakage, odour or contamination, and temperature indication on chilled goods. Only inspected goods are booked into the system for put-away to Zone B, E or F.

7. Chilled and hazardous deliveries are segregated immediately. Chilled goods for Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C are priority-checked and not booked until integrity is confirmed for supervisor decision under PR-12. Hazardous packed goods are checked against papers and labels without opening and held segregated for escorted put-away only to the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage within its 4,000 kg limit under PR-13.

8. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are separated at the time they are found. The operator flags them in the WMS, keeps them out of available stock, and moves them to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found with reference and reason under PR-09. They never enter bulk storage, the cold zone or the pick faces.

9. The operator closes the receipt by confirmation in the WMS. Quantity and condition are confirmed by scan, booking errors stop release for correction with a second count, and Zone A space is cleared and squared for the next booked arrival. Incomplete receipts, held paperwork and quarantine moves are reported to the supervisor.

10. The inbound operator works to site safety and handover discipline throughout. High-visibility vest and class S3 footwear are worn with no exceptions, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, powered trucks are used only if separately authorised under the no licence, no truck rule, and unfinished work, defects and scanner faults are handed over by name under PR-15.

title: Pickers
text:
1. The Pickers are 10 posts working in Zone C picking of 1,200 m2 across the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They report to the shift supervisor in charge and work only against scanner tasks under PR-04 Order picking.

2. Picking takes place only in Zone C on ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk storage. Pickers never pick from Zone B bulk storage, from quarantine in Zone F, from the hazmat cage or the cold zone, and never pick without a WMS task on the 20 handheld scanners.

3. Picking starts only after the faces for the shift have been replenished from Zone B under PR-03. The shift supervisor sequences tasks and does not send pickers to empty or unconfirmed faces, and urgent top-ups during the shift are done only on new WMS tasks by authorised forklift operators.

4. Each scanner task states client, order, product, quantity, batch and expiry where required, pick location in Zone C and destination for packing and Zone D. The picker follows the scanner sequence location by location, confirms the location label first, then picks the stated quantity without substitution or splitting across orders unless tasked.

5. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans the product or carton label and the pick-face label as required, checks quantity, description, batch and expiry on the scanner screen, and confirms only when they agree. Any scan mismatch stops that pick until resolved with the supervisor.

6. Shortages, wrong stock, damaged packaging, unreadable labels or batch and expiry doubts are reported at once. The location is flagged in the WMS and the goods are not packed as good stock. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count by stock controllers.

7. Picked goods are placed cleanly without overhang, crushing or mixing of orders, batches or clients unless the task expressly requires it. Each pallet, load included, respects the site limit of 1,000 kg. Unstable, leaning or damaged pallets are rebuilt or segregated before onward movement.

8. After verification the picker passes goods to packing and labelling under PR-05 and transfer to Zone D under PR-06. Only verified and correctly labelled pallets move to Zone D, where they are stretch-wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic wrappers and staged by door and load. Unverified or unlabelled pallets are never staged for dispatch.

9. Movement from Zone C to Zone D is a WMS task only. Hand-written moves, manual carries without a scan, and staging direct to outbound doors 5–8 without dispatcher release are forbidden. Pickers use hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks for small moves and never operate counterbalance forklifts or reach trucks unless separately authorised under the no licence, no truck rule.

10. The picker works to site safety and handover discipline throughout. High-visibility vest and class S3 footwear are worn with no exceptions, 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers are used for all foot movement, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles are kept clear, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and pick faces are observed, and incomplete tasks, short faces and scanner faults are handed over by name under PR-15.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. The Forklift Operators are 8 posts working across Zones A to F on the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They report to the shift supervisor in charge and work only on WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety.

2. The operators drive the all-electric fleet: 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays in Zone B, and 8 electric pallet jacks for small moves, with 12 hand pallet jacks for light positioning. No diesel or gas-powered truck is used inside the 6,000 m2 hall.

3. The rule is fixed: no licence, no truck. Powered trucks are driven only by persons holding the required licence and current site authorisation, type-specific for counterbalance, reach and electric pallet jack. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises new forklift operators, recorded by name, date, truck types and licence evidence, and no other person grants driving permission.

4. Every truck receives a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned operator checks forks, mast, chains, brakes, steering, hydraulics, wheels, lights, beacon, horn, seat belt and battery, and records truck identity, date, shift and name. An unchecked or defective truck is tagged out with keys removed and reported to the supervisor and maintenance technician.

5. Operators carry out put-away from Zone A, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C, transfer from Zone C to Zone D, and loading and unloading at doors 1–8. Reach trucks alone work inside the high bays within the 10 m clear height; counterbalance forklifts deliver to and collect from the aisle ends. Movement between zones without a scanner task is forbidden.

6. Rated capacities and storage limits are never exceeded. Each pallet, load included, weighs at most 1,000 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and block-stacking is limited to marked areas at 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height. Overweight, leaning, unstable or damaged pallets are refused and go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

7. Speed limits are fixed and enforced: 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard of 3,500 m2, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers and crossings, Zone C pick faces, and dock ramps and leveller areas. Pedestrians have absolute priority and trucks slow, stop, make eye contact and give way.

8. Aisle, load and dock discipline is binding. Operators use 4.0 m main aisles for travel, keep 3.0 m rack aisles fully clear, keep right and stop at intersections, carry loads low at 150–200 mm with clear vision, and serve only the assigned door — 1–4 inbound, 5–8 outbound at 1.2 m dock height — with the trailer braked and secured. Seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving and no passenger is carried.

9. Any impact, overload, near miss, spill, pedestrian breach or truck defect stops work in that aisle, bay or dock. The operator secures the truck clear of aisles and exits, alerts the shift supervisor in charge, and the area stays closed until inspected. Damage is logged by the maintenance technician and driving resumes only after clearance.

10. The operator works to site PPE and handover discipline throughout. High-visibility vest and class S3 footwear are worn with no exceptions, charging is done only in the marked area, and open tasks, defects, bay closures and scanner faults are handed over by name under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Repeated breach, speeding or missed check leads to removal from driving and referral to the Warehouse Manager.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. The Returns and Packing Staff are 4 posts working in Zone F services and control of 600 m2 across the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They report to the shift supervisor in charge and work on WMS tasks under PR-07 Returns handling, PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

2. All returns are received and inspected only in Zone F. Staff accept returns only within 14 days of delivery to the customer, checked by delivery date, return note and WMS order reference on the 20 handheld scanners. Goods outside the window are refused and the refusal is recorded for the dispatcher and supervisor.

3. Every returned unit is inspected, without sampling. Staff check quantity, product identity, packaging, seal integrity, labelling, batch and expiry where required, visible damage, leakage, odour or contamination, and temperature indication on chilled goods. No unit is passed as good stock without this individual check.

4. Returned chilled and hazardous goods are segregated immediately. Chilled units do not re-enter Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C until integrity is confirmed under PR-12. Hazardous packs are checked against papers and labels without opening and go only to the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage within its 4,000 kg limit or to quarantine under PR-13.

5. Staff propose the disposition for every inspected unit — restock, rework or scrap — but do not decide it. Restock is proposed only for clean, intact, labelled goods within date; rework for goods made saleable by re-cartoning, relabelling, re-wrapping or pallet rebuild; scrap for damaged, expired or unverifiable goods. The proposal is presented to the shift supervisor in charge.

6. The final disposition of inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor, who also approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the Warehouse Manager. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count by stock controllers, and no damaged goods leave quarantine without recorded approval.

7. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are quarantined in Zone F the same day they are found. Staff scan pallet or unit and quarantine location, record client, product, quantity, batch and expiry, reference and reason, and flag zero availability for replenishment and picking. Quarantine is never held in Zones A, B, C, D or E.

8. On packing, staff carry out value-added packing, labelling and wrapping support in Zone F and at the Zone C to Zone D interface. Only scan-verified picks are packed to WMS task, labelled by client, order and batch, and stretch-wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic wrappers. Each pallet, load included, respects 1,000 kg, is sound and within footprint, and cardboard waste is fed to the cardboard baler.

9. Movement between zones is by WMS task only. Approved restock moves to Zone B, Zone E or via replenishment to Zone C scan-confirmed at location; approved rework is completed and re-inspected unit by unit before re-presentation. Manual moves without a scan, mixing of orders or batches unless tasked, and use of powered trucks without separate authorisation under the no licence, no truck rule are forbidden.

10. Staff work to site safety and handover discipline throughout. High-visibility vest and class S3 footwear are worn with no exceptions, 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers are used, 4.0 m main aisles are kept clear, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are observed, and inspections, dispositions, quarantine moves and scanner faults are handed over by name under PR-15.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. The Stock Controllers are 2 posts covering inventory accuracy across the 6,000 m2 hall on the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season. They report to the shift supervisor in charge and own cycle counts, recounts and adjustment proposals under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

2. The stock controllers own system accuracy day to day on the principle that system stock is rack stock. They prepare the daily count programme from the WMS, sequence locations with the shift supervisor to avoid blocking put-away from Zone A, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C and staging to Zone D, and record all results by name, date and shift.

3. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Counts cover in turn Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces and flow racks, Zone E cold zone, Zone D staging and Zone F including packing, quarantine, returns and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No zone is omitted from rotation.

4. Each count is a WMS task on the 20 handheld scanners. The task states zone, aisle, bay or location, product, batch and expiry where required, and system quantity. The controller scans the location label then the pallet or product label, counts pallets, cartons and units as tasked, and confirms or flags the result. Counting from memory or without a task is forbidden.

5. No adjustment is ever posted on a first count alone. Every difference — overage, shortage, wrong product, wrong batch or expiry, wrong location, damaged or unlabelled pallet — triggers a mandatory second count by a different person, normally the second stock controller or the shift supervisor, before any correction is proposed.

6. If first and second counts agree, the result is proposed for adjustment with reason and evidence. If they disagree, a third check is ordered by the shift supervisor with the supervisor present. Unresolved locations remain suspended for replenishment and picking and are carried forward, never force-adjusted to system.

7. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming stock found during counts is excluded from available stock. Controllers flag it in the WMS and move it to quarantine in Zone F the same day it is found under PR-09, with reference and photographs where required. Such stock re-enters Zone B, Zone E or Zone C only if inspection and approval later release it as restock.

8. Zone E and hazmat counts follow special discipline. Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C is counted with minimal door-open time, batched locations and alarms plus manual verification each shift continuing. The hazmat cage is counted in place under PR-13 without opening packs, checked against its 4,000 kg limit equivalent to 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, with any leak, odour or damage stopping work for supervisor assessment.

9. Controllers enforce storage limits found during counts and support the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. Any rack bay above 2,700 kg, block stack above 3 pallets high or 4.0 m, pallet above 1,000 kg including load, or unstable pallet is reported to the supervisor, lowered or rebuilt by an authorised operator, and quarantined if damaged. For the annual shutdown they prepare tasks, pair counting teams, and lead recounts; the results are signed personally by the Warehouse Manager.

10. The stock controllers work to site approval, safety and handover discipline throughout. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR await shift supervisor approval and above 500 EUR await Warehouse Manager approval, with no damaged goods leaving quarantine without recorded approval. High-visibility vest and class S3 footwear are worn, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones are observed, and counts, recounts, quarantine moves and scanner faults are handed over by name under PR-15.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. The Maintenance Technician is 1 post covering the safe condition of trucks, racking and dock equipment across the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 fenced yard. The Technician works across the two rostered shifts, mornings 06:00–14:00 and afternoons 14:00–22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for approved Saturday morning overtime in peak season, under the floor authority of the shift supervisor in charge and reporting to the Warehouse Manager.

2. The Technician owns all repairs to materials-handling and site equipment under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. This includes the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays in Zone B, the 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks, dock levellers at all 8 doors at 1.2 m dock height, racking in Zone B, and hardware faults on the 20 handheld WMS scanners. No repair is carried out by unauthorised staff.

3. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day. The assigned authorised operator carries out the check by truck identity and records date, shift, time and name. The Technician reviews missed or failed checks, inspects defects reported by the supervisor, tags out unsafe trucks with keys removed, and returns a truck to service only by recorded release as repaired and safe.

4. Daily checks cover forks, carriage, chains, hoses and mast, wheels and fixings, overhead guard, seat belt and seat switch, lights, beacon, horn and reverse alarm, brakes, steering and hydraulics, and battery charge, connector and cables on the all-electric fleet. Reach trucks receive additional checks for reach, tilt, side-shift, height indicator and 1.6 t plate legibility for work within the 10 m clear height. Any fault in lift, reach or height control stops high-bay work.

5. The Technician carries out the documented racking safety inspection every calendar month together with the shift supervisor in charge. Every rack bay in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions is checked bay by bay for the 2,700 kg total limit, upright and beam damage, missing pins, beam levels, bay labels, and floor markings, with block stacks checked for 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height and aisles for 4.0 m main and 3.0 m rack clearance.

6. Damaged components are red-tagged, offloaded if unsafe, and quarantined from use until repaired. The supervisor stops put-away and picking access to that bay or floor area and secures it with barriers or tape. Work resumes only after clearance is recorded, with WMS locations for blocked bays remaining suspended until release.

7. Dock, barrier and plant maintenance is held to the same discipline. The Technician maintains levellers at doors 1–4 inbound and 5–8 outbound, yellow barriers on 1.2 m pedestrian walkways, floor markings, refrigeration plant, door seals, alarms and temperature displays in Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C, and ventilation, lighting, signage and spill equipment at the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. Charging is confined to the marked ventilated area.

8. Every repair is logged with date, equipment identity, fault description, parts used, work done, downtime and release signature. The log is kept with the daily check sheets and racking logs, reviewed by the supervisor and Warehouse Manager, and unfinished work is handed over by name under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Missing checks, repeated defects, overload damage above 1,000 kg per pallet or impact to uprights and levellers are reported to the Manager.

9. The Technician does not hold manager or supervisor authorities. The Technician does not authorise new forklift operators under the no licence, no truck rule, does not approve overtime, write-offs or return dispositions, and does not release outbound loads or change dispatcher doors and slots. Defects affecting safety, temperature, hazmat containment or evacuation routes are escalated at once through the supervisor to the Manager.

10. The Technician works to site safety and handover discipline throughout. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are worn with no exceptions, 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed, pedestrians on 1.2 m walkways have absolute priority, and open repairs, tagged-out trucks, isolated bays and leveller, alarm or barrier defects are handed over by name under PR-15 until closed.

title: Common Standards for All Roles
text:
1. These standards apply to every person employed at Harborwick 3PL Ltd., about 38-40 staff in total: warehouse manager, 2 shift supervisors, 8 forklift operators, 6 inbound operators, 10 pickers, 2 stock controllers, 4 returns and packing staff, 1 maintenance technician, 2 dispatchers and 2 floaters. No person works outside role, training and authorisation.

2. Standard hours are two fixed shifts, Monday to Friday: mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00. In peak season Saturday morning overtime is added only when approved in advance. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime, and no supervisor, dispatcher or operator authorises additional hours.

3. Reporting lines are fixed on every shift. All floor staff report to the named shift supervisor in charge of the floor, identified at shift start and reachable throughout the shift. The shift supervisor reports to the Warehouse Manager, who is accountable for the whole site and remains accountable where running is delegated.

4. Dispatchers, stock controllers and the maintenance technician work within their own duties but remain under the supervisor's floor authority for safety, traffic and sequencing during the shift. Escalation runs from supervisor to Warehouse Manager, unless immediate escalation is required for injury, evacuation, spill or temperature excursion.

5. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. The rule covers Zones A to F, all aisles, dock interfaces and the yard interface, on both shifts and any approved overtime. No person enters or remains without correct PPE in serviceable condition.

6. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, in addition to vest and footwear. No passenger is carried and no truck moves with an unbelted operator. The shift supervisor stops any person without vest or S3 footwear and any unbelted driving, records the breach by name and refers repeated breaches to the Warehouse Manager.

7. Mandatory induction is completed by every starter on day one: site layout of the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 yard, six zones A to F, doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound, driver waiting discipline, 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in shared areas, and assembly point by the north fence.

8. Mandatory procedural training covers the fifteen procedures PR-01 to PR-15 to the level of the role. All staff are trained in PR-11 pedestrian safety, PR-14 evacuation and PR-15 handover; each role is trained in its own procedures before working unsupervised. Staff work only to the current version and only on WMS tasks on the 20 handheld scanners.

9. Additional authorisation applies to defined work. The rule is no licence, no truck: counterbalance forklifts at 2.5 t, reach trucks at 1.6 t and electric pallet jacks are driven only with licence and current site authorisation granted only by the Warehouse Manager. Every truck receives a documented check before first use each day, and limits of 1,000 kg per pallet, 2,700 kg per bay and 4,000 kg in the hazmat cage are binding on all.

10. Every shift starts with task allocation and ends with formal handover under PR-15. Duties, counts with no adjustment without a second count, quarantine moves the same day damage is found, cold-zone verification at +2 °C to +8 °C, incidents, defects and tagged-out equipment are recorded by name, date and shift. Verbal-only handover is forbidden, and where any manual differs from the owner's brief, the brief prevails.

title: Receiving Hours, Doors and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. receives inbound goods in Zone A during its rostered operating hours: Monday to Friday, morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00. These hours are the contracted receiving window for all clients and carriers, and all inbound bookings, unloading, checking and system booking take place within them.

2. In peak season the company may offer Saturday morning receiving as overtime. Saturday intake is not part of the standard service level and is provided only by prior agreement with the client and only when approved by the warehouse manager. No Saturday arrival is accepted without a confirmed dispatcher booking.

3. Inbound receiving uses doors 1-4 only, serving the 800 m2 Zone A receiving area. All four doors are at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller operated only by trained staff. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and are never used for inbound, and the inbound-outbound separation is guaranteed to clients.

4. Every inbound arrival requires advance booking by the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns a specific inbound door from doors 1-4 and a fixed time slot, and confirms carrier name, trailer reference, client, expected pallet count and any chilled or hazmat flag. No truck is received without a door and slot.

5. Carriers are instructed at booking on door, slot, site speed limits and waiting rules. In the fenced yard of 3,500 m2 vehicles keep to marked lanes at 15 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Early, late or unbooked trucks wait as directed and do not occupy a dock door until called forward.

6. On arrival the driver reports at the assigned inbound door and presents the delivery documents. Drivers then wait in the marked waiting area in the yard and do not enter the hall, storage or picking zones, and do not operate forklifts, pallet jacks, levellers or WMS scanners. Contact takes place at the dock or via the dispatcher.

7. The service commitment for intake is document-check-before-unload. Nothing is unloaded until the inbound operator has checked delivery notes and transport papers against the dispatcher booking for carrier, client, reference, quantity, product, batch and expiry, and cold-chain or hazmat flag, and has confirmed correct door and load.

8. If documents are missing, incomplete or do not match the booking, unloading does not start. The load is held at the dock, the shift supervisor in charge and the dispatcher are informed, and the discrepancy is recorded. Nothing moves past Zone A until the paperwork is resolved, and the client is informed through the dispatcher record.

9. Once documents pass, the company commits to unload, count and inspect in Zone A before booking. Goods are staged by delivery clear of levellers, aisles and walkways, counted by pallet and carton against checked documents, and inspected for packaging, pallet condition, labelling, visible damage and, for chilled goods, temperature indication. Only inspected goods are booked into the WMS.

10. Booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F on WMS tasks, and Zone A is cleared for the next booked arrival. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods found at intake are separated at once and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. They do not enter bulk storage, the cold zone or pick faces as available stock.

title: Dispatch Hours, Capacity and Release
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. dispatches outbound goods from Zone D during its rostered operating hours: Monday to Friday, morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00. These hours are the contracted dispatch window for all clients, and all staging, release, loading and sealing take place within them.

2. In peak season the company may offer Saturday morning dispatch as overtime. Saturday dispatch is not part of the standard service level and is provided only by prior agreement with the client and only when approved by the warehouse manager. No Saturday loading is undertaken without a confirmed dispatcher booking.

3. Outbound dispatch uses doors 5-8 only, serving the 900 m2 Zone D staging area. All four doors are at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own dock leveller operated only by trained staff. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and are never used for outbound, and the inbound-outbound separation is guaranteed to clients.

4. Every outbound departure requires advance booking by the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns a specific outbound door from doors 5-8 and a fixed time slot, and confirms carrier name, trailer reference, client, pallet count and weight, and any chilled or hazmat flag. No truck is loaded without a door, slot and released load.

5. The service commitment for capacity is fixed by dock throughput. Each of the 4 outbound doors handles at most 3 trailer loads per shift, giving 12 trailer loads per shift across the site. This rate applies equally to both rostered shifts and to any approved Saturday overtime, and no commitment beyond it is promised.

6. The service commitment for trailer loads is built on full-weight pallets of 1,000 kg including load. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions, so weight limits each trailer to 24 full-weight pallets. Lighter pallets may use further floor positions up to 33 only while total weight remains within 24,000 kg.

7. On that basis the maximum promise to clients is 288 full-weight pallets per shift: 4 doors multiplied by 3 loads multiplied by 24 pallets. Planning, booking and release never exceed this figure, or the trailer weight and position limits. Any volume above the limit is replanned by the dispatcher to the next slot or trailer.

8. Small consignments use the delivery van rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions. The van carries one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet only, with the balance reserved for packaging and securing. Anything heavier than one full-weight pallet, or beyond the van rating, goes by trailer and is never split to overload the van.

9. The service commitment for release is staged-load-only. Only scan-verified, packed, labelled and stretch-wrapped pallets assigned to the load are staged in Zone D by door and by load on WMS tasks. No truck at doors 5-8 is loaded or sealed until the dispatcher has released the load after weight, count and staging agree.

10. On release the truck is positioned, braked and secured at its assigned door, loaded in sequence with pallets counted and scan-confirmed onto the trailer, then sealed with the seal number recorded and documents handed to the driver at the dock. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area, do not enter the hall, and incomplete loads or door changes are recorded and carried to the next slot.

title: Order Accuracy and Packing
text:
1. The company guarantees that all customer order picking takes place only in the 1,200 m2 Zone C picking area, on ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from bulk storage. No client order is ever picked from Zone B bulk storage, from quarantine in Zone F, or without a WMS task, and this zone discipline is part of the accuracy commitment.

2. The service commitment for availability is replenished faces before picking. Before each picking shift, morning from 06:00 and afternoon from 14:00, the pick faces in Zone C are replenished from Zone B under PR-03 on WMS tasks. Pickers work only against scanner tasks with available stock, and no picker is sent to an empty or unconfirmed face.

3. All picking runs under PR-04 on the 20 handheld WMS scanners. Each task states client, order, product, quantity, batch and expiry where required, Zone C location and destination for packing and Zone D. The picker follows the scanner sequence, confirms the location label first, then picks the stated quantity without substitution.

4. The order accuracy standard is scan-verification of every picked item before it is packed. The picker scans the product or carton label and the pick-face label as required, checks quantity, description, batch and expiry on the scanner screen, and confirms only when they agree. Any scan mismatch stops that pick until resolved with the shift supervisor.

5. Shortages, wrong stock, damaged packaging, unreadable labels or batch and expiry doubts are excluded from good dispatch. The location is flagged in the WMS and the goods are not packed as good stock. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count by stock controllers.

6. Picked goods are handled to preserve accuracy to dispatch. Goods are placed cleanly without overhang, crushing or mixing of orders, batches or clients unless the task expressly requires it, and each pallet, load included, respects the site limit of 1,000 kg. Unstable or damaged pallets are rebuilt or segregated before onward movement.

7. The service commitment for packing runs under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Only scan-verified picks are packed to WMS task, checked for quantity and marking, and closed, sealed and squared by order, batch and client. Manual packing without a scanner task, and hand-written moves without a scan, are forbidden.

8. Every carton, unit and pallet receives its correct outbound identity before it leaves packing. Labels show client, order, destination, quantity and batch and expiry where required, confirmed by scan. Pallets without a correct label and system booking do not move to wrapping or to Zone D and are held in Zone C for correction.

9. All outbound pallets are stretch-wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Wrapping is full, tight and anchored to the pallet base, and unwrapped or poorly wrapped pallets are re-wrapped. Only wrapped, labelled pallets assigned to a released outbound load are staged in Zone D in front of docks 5-8 by door and by load.

10. Transfer from Zone C to Zone D is closed in the WMS when every verified pick is confirmed as packed, labelled, wrapped and staged to its door and load, or flagged as an exception. Incomplete orders, short faces, label errors and scanner faults are recounted and rechecked, handed over by name under PR-15, and faces needing top-up are returned to the replenishment queue.

title: Storage Capacity and Put-Away
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. offers bulk storage in Zone B of 2,200 m2 within the 6,000 m2 hall. The zone holds high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions within 10 m clear height, plus defined free block-stacking areas outside the racking. It is the contracted reserve store for ambient packed consumer goods and feeds the pick faces in Zone C.

2. The service commitment for pallet weight is 1,000 kg per pallet, load included. No pallet accepted for storage exceeds this figure. All rack bay loads, block-stack heights and handling plans are calculated on the basis of full-weight 1,000 kg pallets.

3. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total, including pallets, goods and pallet timber. In practice this means no more than two full-weight pallets per bay, with the balance reserved for weight variation and safe handling. The bay label is never exceeded.

4. Free block-stacking is offered only in marked floor areas outside the racking. Stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and to 4.0 m total height including pallets and load, whichever is reached first. Any stack that would exceed either limit is split and relocated, never topped up.

5. Zone B holds ambient goods only. Goods requiring chill between +2 °C and +8 °C are stored only in the 300 m2 Zone E cold zone, hazardous packed goods only in the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F within its 4,000 kg limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets, and quarantine and returns only in Zone F. No chilled, hazmat or quarantine stock is placed in Zone B to use spare positions.

6. The service commitment for put-away is booked-goods-only under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Only goods that have been counted, inspected and booked into the WMS in Zone A move to Zone B, E or F. Unbooked goods, goods held for paperwork, and damaged or suspect goods are never put away as available stock.

7. Every put-away is a WMS task on the handheld scanners. Each task states client, product, quantity, pallet identity, destination zone and location, and priority. Each booked pallet carries its system label and storage instruction before leaving Zone A, and movement without a scanner task is forbidden.

8. Put-away is sequenced to keep Zone A clear for the next booked arrival. Chilled pallets for Zone E are put away first without delay, hazmat pallets move by escorted transfer to the cage only and only while the 4,000 kg limit allows, and ambient pallets follow to Zone B in booking order under direction of the shift supervisor in charge.

9. Placement is scan-confirmed at the storage location. The operator scans pallet and location labels, confirms upright and beam condition before placing to height, and respects aisle discipline on 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles. Overweight, unstable, damaged or overhanging pallets are refused for height or stack.

10. Put-away is closed in the WMS when all booked pallets of the delivery are confirmed in Zone B, E or F. Booking errors or misplaced pallets are held in Zone A or at location, recounted and corrected before a new task is issued, with no adjustment posted without a second count. Damaged goods found at put-away go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

title: Counts, Adjustments and Reporting
text:
1. The company commits to cycle counts every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. The rotation covers in turn all client stock locations — Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C pick faces and flow racks, Zone E cold zone, Zone D staging and Zone F including quarantine, returns and the ventilated hazmat cage — so that system stock is continuously verified against stock on the rack.

2. Counts are owned day to day by the 2 stock controllers under the shift supervisor in charge. The controllers prepare the daily count list from the WMS, sequence locations to avoid blocking put-away from Zone A, replenishment to Zone C and staging to Zone D, and record every result by name, date and shift. Counting takes place without stopping the contracted inbound and outbound flow.

3. Every count is a WMS task on the handheld scanners. The counter scans the location label then the pallet or product label, counts pallets, cartons and units with batch and expiry where required, and confirms or flags the result in the system. Counting from memory or without a scanner task is forbidden, and matched locations are confirmed as correct in the WMS.

4. Zone E is counted with minimal door-open time to protect storage between +2 °C and +8 °C, with alarms and manual verification each shift continuing in parallel. The hazmat cage in Zone F is counted in place under PR-13 without opening packs, checked against its 4,000 kg limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets. Damaged, leaking or temperature-suspect goods found during any count go to quarantine in Zone F the same day.

5. The service standard for accuracy is no adjustment without a second count. Every difference — overage, shortage, wrong product, wrong batch or expiry, wrong location, damaged or unlabelled pallet — triggers a mandatory recount by a different person, normally the second stock controller or the shift supervisor, before any correction is proposed. Unresolved locations remain suspended for replenishment and picking and are never force-adjusted to system.

6. Once a year the site shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08. All locations in Zones B, C, D, E and F are counted in one exercise with inbound, put-away, replenishment, picking and dispatch frozen and dock bookings at doors 1-4 and 5-8 suspended. The stocktake is planned and ordered by the warehouse manager and covers both rostered shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00.

7. The annual count is carried out by paired teams so that no location is counted and confirmed by the same person, using preloaded tasks on the 20 handheld scanners. Every difference is immediately recounted by a second team before any correction is proposed with reason and evidence. Storage limits found during the stocktake are enforced at once, including 2,700 kg per rack bay, 3 high and 4.0 m for block stacks, and 1,000 kg per pallet.

8. No client stock is adjusted or written off without recorded approval. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor in charge, and any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager after quarantine, inspection and documentation under PR-09. The annual stocktake results are personally signed off by the warehouse manager by name and date.

9. The company reports count performance to the client. Daily cycle-count completions, second counts outstanding and quarantine moves are recorded with WMS references; proposed adjustments state location, product, quantity, batch and expiry, first and second count names, reason and evidence; approved postings, restock, rework or scrap dispositions and the signed annual stocktake summary are made available to the client on request. Reports are issued within the rostered Monday to Friday shifts.

10. All counts, recounts, adjustments and reports are closed in the WMS and handed over by name under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Open recounts, suspended locations, pending approvals above 500 EUR and scanner faults are carried forward to the next shift with an owner. The warehouse manager reviews accuracy data, and where any record differs from the owner's brief on how the site is actually run, the brief prevails.

title: Responsibilities and Governance
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. places final accountability for inventory control and reporting with the warehouse manager as owner of the site. The manager is accountable for operations, safety and inventory accuracy across the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 yard, owns the six-zone layout and procedures PR-01 to PR-15, and remains accountable where daily running is delegated.

2. Each shift is owned on the floor by one named shift supervisor in charge, covering mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, plus cover for any approved Saturday morning overtime. The supervisor allocates tasks, sequences put-away from Zone A, replenishment from Zone B to Zone C, transfer to Zone D and counts, enforces discipline, and hands over formally under PR-15.

3. Dock scheduling and load release are owned by the 2 dispatchers. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot — doors 1-4 inbound only for Zone A, doors 5-8 outbound only for Zone D — and releases outbound loads only when weight, count and staging agree. No other role changes doors, slots or releases.

4. Day-to-day stock accuracy is owned by the 2 stock controllers under the shift supervisor. They prepare the daily cycle-count programme from the WMS, carry out counts and mandatory second counts on the handheld scanners, propose adjustments with reason and evidence, and prepare the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. The principle that system stock is rack stock rests with them.

5. Floor roles work within fixed boundaries under the supervisor. Inbound operators count and inspect in Zone A, pickers pick only scanner tasks in Zone C, forklift operators move only on WMS tasks on checked electric trucks, returns and packing staff inspect in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, and floaters cover only tasks they are trained for.

6. Technical condition is owned by the 1 maintenance technician. The technician maintains trucks, racking with 2,400 positions, levellers at all 8 doors, refrigeration and alarms in Zone E and ventilation in the hazmat cage, carries out the monthly racking inspection with the supervisor, and logs every repair. No repair is made by unauthorised staff.

7. Financial and inventory sign-offs are split by fixed authority. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR, approves the final disposition of inspected returns, and reviews every incident report before close or escalation. Any write-off above 500 EUR and the annual stocktake results are approved and personally signed off only by the warehouse manager.

8. People and hours controls are reserved to the manager. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators under the no licence, no truck rule and only the warehouse manager approves overtime, including Saturday morning overtime in peak season. No supervisor, dispatcher or operator grants driving permission or additional hours.

9. The escalation line for inventory matters is fixed and reported to the client. Count differences, quarantine moves and booking errors go to the stock controllers and shift supervisor; door conflicts, missed slots and load replans go through the dispatcher and supervisor; injury, evacuation, spill, temperature excursion or loss above 500 EUR is escalated without delay to the warehouse manager.

10. Governance is closed by recorded handover and review. Every shift records staffing, doors handled, Zone A to F status, counts and recounts, quarantine and hazmat quantity, incidents and open approvals by name, date and shift under PR-15. The warehouse manager reviews handovers, accuracy data and inspection logs, and where any record differs from the owner's brief on how the site is actually run, the brief prevails.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. holds all damaged, suspect or non-conforming client goods in quarantine in Zone F services and control under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Quarantine is held only in Zone F and never in Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch or Zone E cold zone, and this segregation is guaranteed to the client.

2. Transfer to quarantine takes place the same day the damage is found. This covers inbound damage found in Zone A, picking and packing damage found in Zone C, count differences in Zones B, C, D and E, temperature-suspect chilled goods, leaking hazmat packs, and returns inspection failures. Affected stock is excluded from available stock for replenishment and picking from the moment it is flagged.

3. Every quarantine entry carries full WMS identity on the handheld scanners. The record states client, product, quantity, pallet identity, batch and expiry where required, inbound or order reference, reason, photographs where required, and quarantine status with zero availability. Pallets respect 1,000 kg including load, are stable and within footprint, and are labelled and segregated by reason.

4. Quarantine stock is physically segregated from value-added packing, returns inspection and the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F. Keep-clear zones at the cage door, packing benches, wrappers and 1.2 m pedestrian walkways behind yellow barriers are maintained, and hazardous quarantine remains under PR-13 within the 4,000 kg cage discipline, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets.

5. The service standard for correctness is no adjustment without a second count. Every quarantine quantity is recounted by a different person, normally the second stock controller or the shift supervisor in charge, with both counts recorded by name, date and shift. Unresolved quantities remain suspended and are never force-adjusted to system.

6. No quarantine pallet is moved, reworked, restocked or scrapped without a recorded decision. Returns staff or stock controllers prepare the facts, second count and value and propose restock, rework or scrap, and the authorised approver records the decision in the WMS before any adjustment is posted. Proposal is not approval.

7. Write-off authority offered to the client is split by a fixed threshold of 500 EUR. The shift supervisor in charge approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR and the final disposition of inspected returns. Any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager after quarantine, inspection and documentation.

8. No damaged goods leave quarantine without that recorded approval. Approved restock returns to available stock only by WMS task to Zone B, to Zone E where +2 °C to +8 °C integrity is confirmed under PR-12, or via replenishment to Zone C. Approved rework is completed in Zone F and re-inspected unit by unit, and approved scrap is posted only after recount and value approval.

9. The company reports quarantine performance to the client. Quarantine moves the same day, second counts outstanding, proposals with reason and evidence, value approvals at and above the 500 EUR threshold, and posted restock, rework or scrap dispositions are recorded with WMS references and made available to the client on request. Reports are issued within the rostered Monday to Friday shifts.

10. Quarantine is closed daily in the WMS and handed over by name under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Open quantities, pending second counts, pending approvals above 500 EUR and scanner faults are carried forward to the next shift with an owner and Zone F status. The warehouse manager reviews quarantine and accuracy data, and where any record differs from the owner's brief on how the site is actually run, the brief prevails.

title: Returns Handling
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. accepts client returns for inspection only within 14 days of delivery to the customer under PR-07 Returns handling. The 14-day window is measured by delivery date against return note and WMS order reference, and is a fixed service commitment to the client.

2. All returns are received and inspected only in Zone F services and control. No return is accepted in Zone A receiving, Zone C picking or Zone D dispatch, and no returned pallet is placed direct to Zone B bulk storage, Zone E cold zone or the pick faces before inspection and approved disposition.

3. Returns arrive by booked transport arranged through the dispatcher. The dispatcher assigns a door and fixed time slot, confirms client, order, quantity and any chilled or hazmat flag, and directs the driver to the marked waiting area in the yard. Drivers do not enter Zone F and do not operate warehouse equipment.

4. The service standard for inspection is every unit, without sampling. The 4 returns and packing staff check quantity, product identity, packaging, seal integrity, labelling, batch and expiry where required, visible damage, leakage, odour or contamination, and for chilled goods temperature indication, recorded as a WMS task on the handheld scanners.

5. Returned chilled and hazardous goods receive immediate segregation. Chilled units do not re-enter Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C until integrity is confirmed under PR-12, and hazardous packs are checked against papers and labels without opening and go only to the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage within its 4,000 kg limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets, or to quarantine under PR-13.

6. Goods found damaged, soiled, leaking, temperature-suspect or non-conforming are excluded from available stock from the moment they are flagged. They are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found with WMS quarantine status, reference, reason and photographs where required, and remain suspended for replenishment and picking.

7. The service standard for correctness is no adjustment without a second count. Every return quantity affecting system balance is recounted by a different person, normally a stock controller or the shift supervisor in charge, with both counts recorded by name, date and shift before any correction is proposed.

8. Returns staff propose the disposition for every inspected unit — restock, rework or scrap — but do not decide it. Restock is proposed only for clean, intact, labelled goods within date; rework only for goods made saleable by defined work in Zone F; scrap for damaged, expired or unverifiable goods. Proposal is not approval.

9. Disposition authority offered to the client is fixed. The final disposition of inspected returns is approved only by the shift supervisor in charge, who also approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager after quarantine, inspection and documentation under PR-09, and no damaged goods leave quarantine without that recorded approval.

10. The company reports returns performance to the client and closes every return in the WMS. Inspection results, quarantine moves, second counts, proposals with reason and evidence, value approvals at the 500 EUR threshold, and posted restock, rework or scrap dispositions are recorded with WMS references and made available on request within the rostered Monday to Friday shifts, with open items handed over by name under PR-15.

title: Chilled Storage Service
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. offers chilled storage in Zone E cold zone of 300 m2 within the 6,000 m2 hall. The zone holds only goods requiring chill and no other stock. Ambient goods remain in Zone B, hazardous packed goods remain in the ventilated 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F, and quarantine remains in Zone F outside the cold zone.

2. The service commitment for condition is storage held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times. The range applies to every position in Zone E on both rostered shifts, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00 Monday to Friday, and during any approved Saturday morning overtime. No chilled client product is stored, staged or left in any other zone to use spare capacity.

3. All chilled work runs under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Chilled deliveries are flagged by the dispatcher at booking with client, product and temperature requirement, priority-checked in Zone A for temperature, packaging and condition, booked to Zone E only when integrity is confirmed, and put away direct to Zone E without delay. Any temperature doubt stops booking for decision by the shift supervisor in charge.

4. Temperature in Zone E is monitored by fixed alarms plus a manual verification each shift. The shift supervisor ensures the check is carried out on every shift with measured value, time, zone and name recorded. The record is kept with shift documents, handed over under PR-15, and made available to the client on request within the rostered Monday to Friday shifts.

5. If the temperature reaches or passes outside +2 °C to +8 °C, or any alarm activates, the company holds all chilled movements. The supervisor secures the zone, checks doors and plant, segregates affected stock in the WMS with zero availability, informs the warehouse manager, and suspends put-away, replenishment, picking and dispatch of chilled goods until clearance is recorded. Affected goods are not picked or dispatched without approval.

6. Door and dwell discipline is guaranteed as part of the service. Zone E doors remain closed except for immediate put-away, count, replenishment or picking moves on WMS tasks. Pallets are not staged in the doorway, in transport aisles or in Zone A longer than needed, and chilled pallets are returned to temperature immediately after scan confirmation. Each pallet, load included, respects 1,000 kg.

7. Only authorised operators on checked electric trucks move chilled pallets on the handheld scanners, observing 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps. Chilled picks are packed and transferred to Zone D without delay to protect the chain, and only scan-verified, labelled and wrapped pallets assigned to a dispatcher-released load are staged for outbound doors 5-8.

8. Stock in Zone E is counted on the daily rotating schedule with minimal door-open time, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count by a different person. Counters batch locations and keep doors closed except for immediate access. Damaged, leaking, unlabelled or temperature-suspect goods found during any count or pick are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

9. The maintenance technician maintains the refrigeration plant, door seals, alarms and temperature displays and logs every repair. Any fault, alarm failure, door defect or missed manual verification is reported at once to the shift supervisor and warehouse manager, stops routine chilled put-away until made safe, and is carried by name in the handover until closed and reported to the client where stock is affected.

10. The company reports cold-chain performance to the client and closes every movement in the WMS. Manual verifications, alarms and excursions, quarantine moves, second counts, approvals and the disposition of affected stock as restock or scrap under the 500 EUR write-off rule are recorded with WMS references and made available on request, with open items handed over by name under PR-15. Where any record differs from the owner's brief, the brief prevails.
